previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for elective laparoscopic repair of a symptomatic paraesophageal hernia with gastroesophageal reflux disease. She underwent successful laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair with mesh reinforcement. Postoperatively, she experienced transient left-sided chest pain, which was evaluated and ruled out as cardiac in origin. A small left pneumothorax resolved spontaneously, and bilateral pleural effusions were noted, with the right side increasing slightly, managed conservatively. She progressed from NPO to clear liquids on postoperative day one and advanced to a regular diet by day three. Her pain was well controlled, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow a modified soft diet, continue home medications including diuretics for heart failure, and monitor for warning signs requiring urgent evaluation. Follow-up was arranged with surgery and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___ at 13:57 hours.

HISTORY:  Chest pain.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Linear scarring at the right lung base and along the right lateral
hemithorax is again present.  Subsegmental atelectasis at the left lung base
is now present with associated left lung volume loss.  No consolidation or
edema is noted.  There is aortic tortuosity.  The cardiac silhouette size is
enlarged and exaggerated.  There is somewhat globular appearance of the heart
and an underlying pericardial effusion which has developed cannot be entirely
excluded.  There are bilateral pleural effusions.  No pneumothorax is seen. 
Multilevel wedge deformities throughout the lower thoracic spine is again
present and relatively stable.

IMPRESSION:  There is interval enlargement of the cardiac silhouette even
accounting for decrease in lung volumes.  The morphology suggests there may be
underlying pericardial effusion.  There are new bilateral pleural effusions
and subsegmental atelectasis of the left lower lobe.

INDICATION:  Left pleural effusion, evaluate for loculation.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___ at 13:57.

LEFT LATERAL DECUBITUS VIEW OF THE CHEST:  Again noted is a small left pleural
effusion, which does not layer freely, suggesting component of loculation. 
Again noted is atelectasis within the left lung base.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Pleural and pericardial effusion, status post pericardial drain
placement, evaluation for interval change.

COMPARISON:  The examination is compared with ___.

FINDINGS:  New placement of a pericardial drain.  The drain appears to be
correctly positioned.  Minimally increasing left and moderate right pleural
effusion.  Subsequent areas of atelectasis that are unchanged as compared to
the previous examination.  Unchanged moderate cardiomegaly, no newly appeared
focal parenchymal opacities suggesting pneumonia.

CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST DATED ___

Comparison studies including chest CT, ___, cardiac CTA of ___, and MR of the abdomen, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric, multidetector CT acquisition of the chest was
performed following 75 cc of intravenous Optiray.  The patient experienced an
anaphylactic reaction following intravenous contrast administration, requiring
treatment with epinephrine.  Dr. ___ monitored the patient during the
contrast reaction and has entered a formal note in the ___ medical record. 
Please see that document for details.

FINDINGS:  Small dependent left pleural effusion and trace amount of right
pleural effusion are new compared to cardiac CTA of ___.  The
effusions measure simple fluid density.  Also new is a small pericardial
effusion as well as pneumopericardium with adjacent soft tissue stranding. 
This is reportedly related to recent pericardial drainage procedure.  Heart is
enlarged but unchanged in size.  Diffuse coronary artery calcifications are
present.  Ascending aorta is mildly dilated at 4.3 cm, similar to prior study
of ___.  Right lower lobe is nearly completely collapsed without
evidence of a centrally obstructing lesion.  The superior segment of the right
lower lobe is partially aerated.  There is also partial atelectasis of the
left lower lobe.  Minimal emphysema is present.  Small amounts of dependent
atelectasis are present in the upper lobes, subsegmental in degree.  Scattered
areas of subsegmental atelectasis are also present in the lingula and right
lower lobe.

The exam was not specifically tailored to evaluate the subdiaphragmatic
region, but note is made of atrophy of the right kidney, similar in appearance
to the prior CT of ___.  Hiatal hernia is present as well as
apparent postoperative changes in region of the gastroesophageal junction. 
Known cystic lesion in the uncinate process of the pancreas was not included
within the imaging acquisition of the study but has been previously evaluated
by MRI of the abdomen.

Note is made of apparent previous left mastectomy procedure.

Healed rib fractures are present.  Note is also made of mild compression
deformities in the spine with similar appearance on prior studies.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Small left pleural effusion has simple fluid characteristics and does not
demonstrate CT findings associated with empyema.  However, direct correlation
with thoracentesis may be helpful to better ascertain the etiology of the
effusion if warranted clinically.
2.  Pericardial fluid and pneumopericardium, the latter reportedly related to
recent drainage procedure.
3.  Bilateral lower lobe atelectasis, right greater than left, with near
complete collapse of right lower lobe.
